newsitem.title: USA: U.S. June S&P 500s finish at all-time highs.
newsitem.headline: U.S. June S&P 500s finish at all-time highs.

text.p: U.S. June Standard & Poor's 500s finished at all-time highs on strong flight-to-quality buying into U.S. asset markets, traders and analysts said.
"It's just like a run-away train," one S&P futures trader said. "With good news or bad news this thing just keeps pounding higher."

S&P futures held only minor losses on the strong U.S. employment numbers, but surged on rumors that the start of the European monetary union (EMU) would be delayed. A delay in EMU exacerbated speculation that the road to a single currency would be fraught with political and economic instability.

Flight-to-quality buying started in the T-bond market, and immediately filtered into the S&P pit. June S&Ps' rally to the GLOBEX high of 851.50 was enough to catch many traders and analysts, most of whom were looking for a subdued day of range trading, by surprise.
"We reversed the breakdown, and traded up, back through the pennant formation that we started modestly breaking through last week," one S&P technician said.
The pennant formation rested slightly below the previous all-time high of 854.70, and corresponded with a double top at Thursday's high of 851.30 and the GLOBEX high.
"People had bets after the employment numbers that the market would trade lower to steady after the reports, but those bets were poorly placed," one S&P futures trader said.
U.S. May nonfarm payrolls rose 138,000, lower than average analysts' estimates of 219,000, but April payrolls were upwardly revised to show a gain of 323,000 from 142,000.
The jobless rate fell to 4.8 percent, its lowest level since October 1973 and against average estimates for a rise to 5.0 percent from 4.9 percent in April.
However, the rumors about EMU overwhelmed the U.S. economic front.
June S&Ps ran through 854.70, triggering technical alerts on the black boxes of many hedge funds and asset allocators.
"When you start trading more technical than rational, the guy with the shorts can only endure so much pain," he said about the market's lack of a pullback.
Both locals and funds were forced to cover short positions, with one fund manager alone buying 1,000 June around midsession.
"With all the sideways action in the last week to 10 days, you had a lot of people short," Daniel Riley, director of institutional trading at Chicago Execution Corp, said.
Traders and analysts said the next major upside objectives for June rested at 868.00, 880.00 and 888.00 to 900.00.

Despite the sharp rally, volume was light and dealers were tentative for most of the day, market sources said. Arbitrage sell programs were noted in the morning when June S&Ps traded at a premium of 0.90 to cash.

At the end of pit trade, June S&Ps were up 16.50 at 862.50, new composites were up 7.45 at 450.60, KCBT Value Lines rose 7.00 at 769.00, Nikkeis were 70 higher at 20,620, Nasdaq 100s rose 15.00 at 948.75 and Russell 2000s were 4.75 higher at 391.00.
